question: Can few-shot visual concepts be learned as executable programs that generalize compositionally, remain inspectable, and permit targeted human repair?

key_findings.claim: Pix2Code turns object-centric scenes into lambda-calculus classifiers using a learned wake-sleep program library.
key_findings.evidence: A pretrained object extractor emits discrete object attributes; beam-guided synthesis composes base and learned primitives into a program that both classifies images and explicitly represents the inferred concept.

key_findings.claim: Program structure supports stronger compositional and entity generalization than the neural CURI baseline in the reported synthetic tests.
key_findings.evidence: Pix2Code beats CURI-B on seven of eight CURI compositional splits and retains 100% accuracy for AllCubes scenes with 5, 8, and 10 objects, while CURI-B falls toward 56%; unsolved synthesis tasks are conservatively scored as random in Acc@all.

key_findings.claim: Readable programs make specific repairs possible, but the demonstrations require a human to identify and encode the correction.
key_findings.evidence: Removing cyan/color primitives restores 100% accuracy on a confounded task and adding four hand-written counting primitives raises counting accuracy near 90%; real-image trials synthesize programs for five of seven COCO concepts.

method.core_idea: Combine neural object extraction with DreamCoder-style library learning so visual relational concepts are executable symbolic programs.
method.mechanism: Discrete bounding-box and attribute tokens define tasks; a learned code model guides enumerative search over a lambda-calculus DSL, while wake-sleep alternates program discovery, library abstraction, and recognition-model training.
assumptions: The object extractor supplies accurate, discretized objects and attributes.
The DSL contains or can be augmented with primitives needed for target concepts.
Support examples distinguish the intended rule from shortcuts within the search budget.

techniques.role: Converts pixels into finite object sequences usable by synthesis.
Discovers reusable program fragments and trains a proposal model.
Repairs confounders or missing operations by deleting or adding primitives.

evaluations.setting: Relational Kandinsky Patterns and CURI iid tasks
evaluations.result: Pix2Code reports 90.05% Acc@all on RelKP and 71.54% on CURI, versus 59.69% and 66.68% for CURI-B; solved-task accuracy is higher but excludes search failures.

evaluations.setting: CURI compositional splits and unseen object counts
evaluations.metric: Median class-balanced accuracy and entity extrapolation
evaluations.result: Pix2Code wins seven of eight composition splits and remains strong as scenes grow to ten objects; counting is the principal weak split before revision.
evaluations.baseline: CURI-B trained to accept up to ten objects

evaluations.setting: Human revision and seven MS COCO concepts
evaluations.metric: Post-repair query accuracy and synthesized-program test accuracy
evaluations.result: Targeted library edits repair two demonstrated failures; programs are found for five COCO concepts, with accuracy from 0.6813 to 0.9324.
evaluations.baseline: Unrevised Pix2Code and original target rules

limitations: Pix2Code depends on discrete object extraction and does not model perceptual uncertainty.
Enumerative synthesis is slow: reported CURI training is about 13.5 hours versus 18 minutes for CURI-B, and many CURI tasks remain unsolved.
Repairs require a person to recognize the shortcut and author an appropriate symbolic intervention; natural-image evidence covers only seven concepts.
failure_modes: Search returns no program within the timeout or chooses a support-set shortcut.
Missing DSL operations make valid concepts inexpressible until manually added.
Noisy or incomplete detections prevent any exact program from separating examples.
reusable_insights: Report synthesis coverage separately from accuracy conditional on finding a program.
Entity-count extrapolation tests symbolic semantics more directly than random iid splits.
Human-editable representations should be evaluated by executing concrete repairs, including their labor and side effects.
open_questions: Can probabilistic object representations and soft program execution tolerate real detector uncertainty?
Can search and library learning scale to open-vocabulary relations without hand-designed integer DSLs?
How should a system surface ambiguous shortcuts and request the smallest human intervention?

competitive_landscape.title: DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Pix2Code adopts wake-sleep library induction but adds a neural perception interface, visual few-shot tasks, and explicit human revision experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: CURI: A Benchmark for Productive Concept Learning Under Uncertainty
competitive_landscape.difference: CURI studies neural productive concept learning; Pix2Code represents concepts as programs and extends evaluation to unseen entity counts and manual repair.

competitive_landscape.title: The Neuro-Symbolic Concept Learner: Interpreting Scenes, Words, and Sentences From Natural Supervision
competitive_landscape.difference: NS-CL learns visual concepts aligned with language and executes programs for questions; Pix2Code induces relational concept programs from positive/negative image sets without language labels and learns reusable library fragments.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: object-centric neuro-symbolic reasoning, DreamCoder, and CURI all predate Pix2Code. Its distinct combination is visual concept induction as learned-library program synthesis, evaluated for compositional/entity extrapolation and executable human repair.
reviewer_notes: Main text and supplements were checked, including coverage accounting, runtime, object-count tests, CURI-Hans repair, counting repair, translations, and COCO failures. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23.
